scouting_result.scout_verdict:
Your 178cm, 76kg frame is a testament to the classic sprinter’s architecture—compact, efficient, and densely packed with the fast-twitch muscle fibers required to explode from the blocks. At 25 years old, you are entering the prime of your career, and your lifelong commitment to structured field training gives you the tactical maturity to match your impressive baseline speed. As you set your sights on the track at The Brisbane 2032 Games, your path is defined by pure, unadulterated output; your ability to convert raw power into velocity is your greatest competitive asset.

In the adaptive arena, the T44 classification specifically accommodates athletes with a lower-limb impairment who compete standing, often utilizing high-tech carbon-fiber prosthetics that mimic the elasticity and energy return of human tendons. Your background in high-intensity sprinting translates seamlessly here. Because you already understand the mechanics of force application and track-specific reactivity, transitioning to a T44 pathway isn't about learning to sprint—it is about mastering the unique rhythm of your gear to ensure that your explosive starts result in world-class acceleration.

scouting_result.scout_verdict:
While your sprinting history is rooted in the linear pursuit of power, the Edge Carver profile pivots to the complex, high-velocity environment of winter speed disciplines. This is where your focus shifts from sheer output to the art of technical management—navigating the delicate threshold between edge grip and centrifugal force. At The Brisbane 2032 Games, this profile positions you as a tactician of speed, where your lifelong discipline allows you to break down every turn into a precise, calculated movement rather than just a brute-force exertion.

The LW12 classification is reserved for sit-skiers with lower-limb impairments who demonstrate elite trunk stability and core strength. This is where your secondary athletic dimension emerges; whereas sprinting demands explosive bursts, the sit-ski requires a profound level of core-driven coordination and spatial awareness to maintain balance at high velocities. By applying your existing reactive speed to the icy lines of a Super-G course, you transform your athletic identity from a straight-line powerhouse into a master of momentum, utilizing your core control to carve the mountain with absolute precision.
